rendered: The premise does not match the document. It does not say bare Al outperformed the carbon/Al collector at 4 mA/cm^2[1]. It reports the reverse: bare Al electrodes were prone to failure at these currents, while the carbon/Al electrodes avoided that failure.[2][3] The document credits the carbon nucleation layer instead. It lowers the nucleation overpotential, from 19 to 12 mV[4], and it gives a mechanically stable interface, so the sodium does not delaminate from the collector as it did on bare Al.[5][6] On hysteresis: the carbon/Al electrode shows a hysteresis of 45 mV[7] at 4 mA/cm^2[8]. The document gives no hysteresis value for bare Al at that current, because bare Al failed there, so the size of any difference cannot be computed. The only hysteresis comparison at that current is with previous work using Cu electrodes, which the authors say reported nearly double the hysteresis at[9] the carbon/Al value at that current. That comparison is to Cu from earlier work, not to bare Al in this study.
